root_cause.text: The s390 syscall dispatch code lacks a speculation barrier (array_index_nospec) after the bounds check on the user-controlled syscall number, allowing speculative out-of-bounds access to the sys_call_table pointer array and enabling Spectre v1 side-channel attacks.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `nr = array_index_nospec(nr, NR_syscalls);` inside the `if (likely(nr < NR_syscalls))` block, and the CVE description states that the syscall number "does not have an array_index_nospec() boundary to prevent access past the syscall function pointer tables."

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `nr = array_index_nospec(nr, NR_syscalls);` inside the `if (likely(nr < NR_syscalls))` block, and the CVE description states that the syscall number "does not have an array_index_nospec() boundary to prevent access past the syscall function pointer tables."

candidates.rationale: Preceding conditional branch that may also be speculated, part of the syscall dispatch flow, but not directly related to the syscall number bounds check vulnerability.
Branch target that speculatively might be taken, but not directly involved in the out-of-bounds access; part of the overall control flow.
Default error code assignment that is overwritten if the bounds check is speculatively bypassed, but the vulnerability is not in this assignment itself.

Bounds check on user-controlled syscall number; without a speculation barrier (array_index_nospec) after this condition, speculative execution can bypass the check and proceed to out-of-bounds array access.
Array access using the user-controlled syscall number as index; speculative execution can use an out-of-bounds index to access sys_call_table, enabling Spectre v1 side-channel attacks.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement directly performs an array access on sys_call_table using the user-controlled syscall number 'nr' as index. Because there is no speculation barrier after the preceding bounds check, speculative execution can use an out-of-bounds index to access memory beyond the array, enabling Spectre v1 side-channel attacks.

This bounds check on the user-controlled syscall number is intended to prevent out-of-bounds access, but it lacks a speculation barrier (array_index_nospec). Speculative execution can bypass this check, allowing the subsequent array access to proceed with an out-of-bounds index.

This assignment sets the default return value to -ENOSYS. While not directly vulnerable, it is part of the same speculative code path: if the bounds check is speculatively bypassed, this assignment is overwritten, and the array access executes. It is included as it is part of the vulnerable control flow.

This conditional branch checks for a return flag. While not directly related to the syscall number vulnerability, it is part of the same syscall dispatch function and could be speculated to influence control flow. It is included as part of the broader speculative context of the vulnerable code region.

This goto statement is the target of the preceding conditional branch. It is part of the speculative execution path; if mis-speculated, it could affect subsequent execution, though its direct role in the out-of-bounds access is minimal. Included for completeness of the vulnerable code block.
